resource.name: aws-s3
resource.description: Amazon S3 object storage used for files uploaded within a project — images, PDFs, documents and other attachments. Files are never proxied through application servers; browsers upload and download directly against S3 using short-lived presigned URLs.

config.description: Access key ID for an IAM principal with PutObject/GetObject (and optionally DeleteObject) permission on the bucket.
AWS region the bucket lives in, e.g. us-east-1.
Secret access key paired with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.
Name of the S3 bucket files are stored in.

resource.consumptionInstructions: A consuming service generates presigned URLs server-side with the AWS SDK — a PutObject presigned URL when a file needs to be uploaded, a GetObject presigned URL when a file needs to be viewed or downloaded — and returns only that URL to the browser, which performs the upload/download directly against S3. Never route file bytes through the application backend, and never hand the browser a long-lived credential: only the service holds the AWS access key and secret, and every presigned URL is scoped to one object key with a short expiry (a few minutes for uploads, longer for read-only viewing links as needed). Object keys should be namespaced per project/tenant to avoid collisions, and the bucket should have public access blocked — the presigned URL is what authorizes each individual request.
